title: AI-assisted driving playtest: separating unclear controls from deliberate difficulty
author: No_Swan7689
selftext:
I'm developing Last Delivery, an arcade driving playtest in Godot, with substantial ChatGPT/Codex assistance for code, code-drawn visuals, text and synthesized audio. No live generative AI runs during play.



You collect parcels and match their colours and shapes to delivery bays. A larger load earns more but makes the trailer harder to steer. That creates a testing problem: a difficult corner might be the intended trade-off, or it might mean the controls or objective weren't clear enough.



I'm keeping the next feedback check small instead of asking people to assess the whole campaign: Driver School, then one delivery. Can a first-time player work out the pickup and matching bay? Once that is clear, does the heavier load feel like a choice or an unfair surprise?



The current R6 browser build includes colour-and-shape cargo badges, matching-bay highlights and simpler Driver School lessons. Those are things to test, rather than proof that the onboarding is solved. I'd like to hear how other AI-assisted developers separate clarity problems from intentional difficulty before changing their handling code again.



Free browser playtest: [https://mogamez.itch.io/last-delivery-playtest](https://mogamez.itch.io/last-delivery-playtest)



Choose Run game, then Load game. Please include your device/browser and control mode if you report a confusing moment. Physical-phone handling still needs testing; the downloadable Android build is older than the browser version. This request is for the browser playtest.



I'm the creator. Optional tips are enabled on [itch.io](http://itch.io), but no payment, download or recording is needed to try the browser game.
